extracted.intended_audience: registered patent agents and other practitioners before the USPTO (respondents/subjects of OED disciplinary proceedings)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedural rules, and sanctions governing practitioner conduct before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office, with particular focus on unauthorized trademark practice, applicable disciplinary rules, and the procedures and remedies available to the OED Director and the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to practice trademark matters before the Office (37 C.F.R. § 11.14(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who are not attorneys are not recognized to practice before the Office in trademark and other non-patent matters, and registration as a patent agent does not itself entitle an individual to practice before the Office in trademark matters. See 37 C.F.R. § 11.14(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is an exception for non-attorneys who were recognized to practice before the Office in trademark matters prior to January 1, 1957, but that exception is not applicable in this disciplinary proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only individuals qualified under 37 C.F.R. § 11.14 may represent parties in trademark cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Only an individual qualified to practice under 37 C.F.R. § 11.14 may represent an applicant, registrant, or party to a proceeding before the Office in a trademark case. See 37 C.F.R. § 2.17(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of practice in trademark matters (37 C.F.R. § 11.5(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice before the Office in trademark matters includes, but is not limited to, consulting with or giving advice to a client in contemplation of filing a trademark application with the Office; preparing and prosecuting an application for trademark registration; preparing an amendment that may require written argument to establish the registrability of the mark; and conducting an opposition, cancellation, or concurrent use proceeding; and conducting an appeal to the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The listed activities are illustrative of what constitutes 'practice' for purposes of authorization requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on holding oneself out as authorized to practice trademark law when not authorized
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner who is not an attorney and not otherwise qualified to practice under 37 C.F.R. § 11.14 may not hold himself out to clients or to the Office as authorized to practice before the Office in trademark cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example factual misconduct: preparing and filing trademark applications and responses while not authorized, and representing to clients and the Office that one is authorized (the respondent prepared and filed at least seventy‑eight trademark applications and held himself out as authorized).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) — dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation, e.g., representing oneself to be a person authorized to practice trademark law before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violation of this rule supports disciplinary action; it was cited as a legal conclusion based on the stipulated facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) — conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct that adversely reflects on a practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office, e.g., intentionally engaging in the practice of trademark law before the Office and/or not realizing that one was not authorized to engage in that practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule may be applied whether the misconduct was intentional or due to a practitioner's failure to recognize lack of authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions: suspension, limited recognition, compliance, probation, and reinstatement timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practicing patent law before the USPTO for thirty-six (36) months commencing on the date the Final Order is signed; granted limited recognition to practice for thirty (30) days solely to facilitate compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b); must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; and shall serve a thirty-six (36) month period of probation beginning on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent may file a petition for reinstatement after twelve (12) months from the date the Final Order is signed pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, but remains suspended unless and until the OED Director grants reinstatement per 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(c). Limited recognition is time‑limited and strictly for compliance with § 11.58(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and process for alleged noncompliance during probation (Order to Show Cause and further suspension/bar)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes the Respondent failed to comply with the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule during probation, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause (OSC) and: (A) if Respondent not yet reinstated, seek an order barring Respondent from filing a request for reinstatement during the thirty‑six month suspension; or (B) if Respondent has been reinstated, seek an order immediately suspending Respondent for up to an additional twenty‑four (24) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OSC shall be sent to the Respondent's last address of record; Respondent is granted fifteen (15) days to respond; after response and consideration, if OED Director remains of that opinion, the OED Director delivers the OSC, response, and evidence to the USPTO Director and requests appropriate action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural limits on review of USPTO Director orders
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director enters an order barring reinstatement or immediately suspending the Respondent and the Respondent seeks review of that action, any such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the USPTO Director's order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of Customer Numbers and CPKI certificates upon additional suspension or bar
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director enters an order barring Respondent from filing a request for reinstatement during the suspension or enters an order immediately suspending Respondent, then: (i) the USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO Customer Numbers and Public Key Infrastructure (CPKI) certificates and (ii) Respondent may not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a direct operational consequence affecting electronic credentials and access to USPTO systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish this Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (http://des.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp) and publish a notice materially consistent with the Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted for public reading at the OED Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may seek further discipline and consider this record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Proposed Settlement Agreement or this Final Order shall prevent the Office from seeking discipline against the Respondent in accordance with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34 through 11.57 for the misconduct that caused amendment and immediate suspension; and the Office may consider the record of this disciplinary proceeding (including this Final Order) when addressing further complaints or in any future disciplinary proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record may be used (i) as an aggravating factor in determining discipline to be imposed and/or (ii) to rebut statements or representations by or on Respondent's behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for dismissal of pending disciplinary proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Within thirty (30) days of the date on which this Final Order is signed, the OED Director shall file a motion to dismiss the disciplinary proceeding currently pending against Respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating consideration: respondent's age and expected remaining career time
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is over 70 years of age, and the terms of the agreed upon settlement took into account the time reasonably expected to be remaining in his career as a patent agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Age and remaining career expectancy were expressly considered in formulating the agreed sanction.
